criteria: useful_findings: did this finding genuinely help, or would a mixing engineer already know/ignore it?
false_flags: did the engine flag something that isn't really a problem in this mix?
missed_problems: did you hear a real technical issue the engine didn't flag at all?
confusing_wording: was any finding's explanation unclear or could it mislead a non-expert?
should_have_abstained_but_didnt: did the engine make a claim it didn't have enough evidence for?
scoring_scale: For useful_findings/false_flags/missed_problems/confusing_wording/should_have_abstained_but_didnt: fill with a short list of specific findings/timestamps, or an empty list/'none' if not applicable. Use notes for anything else.
instructions: For each case, listen to the actual mix (paths supplied separately, out of this JSON) and compare against the engine's findings above. Score each of the 5 criteria per case. This qualifies the *current* fault-family set (clipping, headroom, silence/truncation, channel imbalance, phase/polarity, DC offset, loudness estimate, calibrated LUFS, true-peak) against real listening judgment -- it does not and cannot evaluate masking, tonal balance, arrangement, or genre-context claims, since KENN does not measure those yet (see explicitly_not_evaluated per case).
limitations: This is a small (11-case) curated sample, not a statistically powered benchmark.
All 11 cases came from AutoMix-rendered or raw stem content from the same test corpus; results may not generalize to hand-mixed commercial masters from other genres/engineers.
A single reviewer's judgment is a data point, not proof; the plan calls for at least two independent reviewers.
